title_en: The government of the United States has banned DJI, but the police of the United States are using it. DJI is really proud this time. On August 14, the U.S. Court of Appeals ruled that the Pentagon’s blacklisting of DJI as a “Chinese military enterprise” lacked sufficient evidence and remanded the case for retrial. This is the first crack China’s hard technology has dug in the iron curtain of sanctions. But what’s even more exciting than the courts is America’s grassroots. The Santa Barbara Fire Department used a DJI thermal imaging drone to pick up a sinking surfer from the Pacific Ocean; the Houston Police Department established a new tactical unit, and the core equipment is the DJI Matrice 4T, which has stronger performance and is only half the price of American products; the Irvine Police Department in California has held its open days for two consecutive years, and all the drones on display are DJI. More than 80% of law enforcement and emergency agencies in the United States use DJI technology, accounting for 70 to 90% of the commercial market. Four out of every five agricultural drones are DJI. It's not that they don't want to buy American products, but they can't afford them - the same functions are three to five times more expensive, and the performance can't keep up. In June 2024, two executives of a Chinese medical company were deceived into the Philippines and then kidnapped. After the family paid a ransom of 3 million, they were expelled. The main criminal, Liu Mouwen, was a mainlander and later fled to the United States. The United States arrested him in October 24 and handed him over to China in July 26. According to reports, Liu Mouwen found a Taiwanese girl and infiltrated a cardiovascular medical academic conference in Europe. The two murdered medical device company executives also attended the conference, and were immediately targeted by the Taiwanese girl. It is said that the Taiwanese girl is very familiar with the industry terminology and procurement model of cardiovascular consumables. This may be an important reason why the two executives did not suspect her. They believed that she was a professional and would not seek money or death. The Taiwanese girl lied that the boss behind her was a very powerful Chinese businessman in the Philippines, saying that she had many large purchase orders for medical equipment from public hospitals in the Philippines.
